metaTitle: Corporate Dessert Boxes and Office Dessert Cups
metaDescription: Corporate dessert boxes of hand-layered cups for office celebrations, client meetings and team thank-yous. Packs of 24, 48 or 96, made fresh in Hamilton.
h1: Corporate dessert boxes, hand-layered for the office
intro: Office celebrations, client meetings, a thank-you for the team that carried the quarter. Our corporate dessert boxes are packs of 24, 48 or 96 hand-layered dessert cups or mini dessert shots, made in Hamilton, Ontario. If you're the one placing the office order, here's how to pick a size and a pack, plan around allergens for a mixed team, and what happens after you hit send.

sections.heading: Office dessert cups: nothing to slice, nothing to plate
sections.body:
A sheet cake needs a knife, a stack of plates and a volunteer willing to cut it in front of the whole department. Every cup here is individually portioned. People take one, eat it standing up or carry it back to their desk, and the table clears itself.

Pick the mix by how it will look in the room. For a client table, [Ferrero Royale](/menu/ferrero-royale)'s dark glossy ganache next to [Dubai Chocolate](/menu/dubai-chocolate)'s green marbled swirl looks polished. For a team celebration, [Mango Dream](/menu/mango-dream)'s saffron orange beside [Strawberry Fields](/menu/strawberry-fields)' glossy red is bright and loud. If your company colours run warm, [Biscoff Bliss](/menu/biscoff-bliss)'s caramel-tan and amber sit in that range. If they run cool, try [Blueberry Haze](/menu/blueberry-haze)'s lilac cream and near-black violet compote.

Four layers, no shortcuts.

sections.heading: Mini Shots or Dessert Cups: pick by the moment
sections.body:
Both sizes come in packs of 24, 48 or 96. The size decides what dessert is doing in the room.

Mini Shots (2 oz) are a tasting size. They sit well beside the coffee at a client meeting or on the side of a catered lunch, where dessert is a nice finish rather than the point.

Dessert Cups (5 oz) are a full serving. Choose them when dessert is the event: a team thank-you, a farewell, a milestone.

Prices start from $45 for 24 Classic Mini Shots, and from $99 for 24 Classic Dessert Cups. Classic and Premium flavours mix freely in the same pack, and a mixed pack is priced cup by cup at each tier's rate: twelve Classic and twelve Premium Dessert Cups in a 24 come to $114 before any delivery fee. Every pack, size and tier is priced on [our packages page](/packages).

sections.heading: Three office moments, three starting points
sections.body:
These are suggestions, not rules. They assume one Dessert Cup or about two Mini Shots per person, so adjust for your headcount.

**Client meeting.** A 24 of Mini Shots in four flavours, six of each, is about two each for a room of 12. A couple of tasting-size cups next to the coffee feel considered without taking over the agenda. Save them for after the decisions are made. [Start with a 24 of Mini Shots](/order?pack=24&size=2oz&event=corporate)

**Team thank-you.** A 48 of Dessert Cups gives a team of up to 48 a full serving each, across as many as eight flavours. There's a ready-made split for it below. [Start with a 48 of Dessert Cups](/order?pack=48&size=5oz&event=corporate)

**Office celebration or client event.** For a whole floor, an all-hands or a room full of guests, the 96 holds up to 16 flavours, with a presentation tray available at extra cost. That's one Dessert Cup each for up to 96 people, or about two Mini Shots each for 48, and it needs at least 7 days' notice. Feeding more than 96? There's no maximum: order more than one pack, as long as each meets the minimums. The form takes one pack at a time, so mention the extra packs in your notes or send another request. [Start with a 96](/order?pack=96&event=corporate)

sections.heading: The 48: priority preparation and a ready-made mix
sections.body:
The 48 is our most popular pack, and it comes with priority preparation. At work you're choosing for forty people and know the tastes of about four of them, so a spread across both tiers is the safe bet.

A 48 holds up to eight flavours, ordered in sixes (6, 12, 18 and so on). One way to split it evenly between the tiers: Mango Dream and Strawberry Fields at six each and Blueberry Haze at twelve for the Classic half, then six each of Kinder Bueno, Ferrero Royale, Biscoff Bliss and Dubai Chocolate for the Premium half. That's seven of the eight flavours a 48 can hold. Browse [the full menu](/menu) if you'd rather choose yourself.

sections.heading: The 96: a label option and event-day pickup
sections.body:
For the bigger occasions, like a company anniversary, a client open house or an all-hands, the 96 comes with a custom label option and event-day pickup. A presentation tray isn't included, but you can request one at extra cost.

A 96 needs at least 7 days' notice and isn't offered on shorter notice, so book it as soon as the date is on the calendar. It's packed as four boxes of 24 cups, without lids, which is worth knowing if a colleague is carrying it in. We'll go over how event-day pickup works when we confirm your order. Like every order, the cups are made fresh the morning of pickup or delivery.

The custom label option is worth asking about when the cups are going in front of clients. Describe what you have in mind in your notes, and we'll confirm what's possible when we reply.

sections.heading: Planning around allergens for a mixed team
sections.body:
Office orders feed people you may not know well, so sort out allergens before you pick flavours, not after the pack is open.

Mango Dream, Strawberry Fields, Blueberry Haze and Biscoff Bliss aren't flagged for tree nuts on our menu. Cross-contact is still possible, so this works for preference, not for an allergy.

On the table, group Kinder Bueno, Ferrero Royale and Dubai Chocolate, the three flavours with tree nuts, and set a small card beside them.

{{dietaryClaim}}

If anyone in the room has a severe allergy, or avoids gluten or egg for medical reasons, message us before you order. More on allergens is in [the FAQ](/faq).

sections.heading: Timing an office order
sections.body:
48 hours is the minimum notice for a 24 or a 48. Requests for those packs with less than 48 hours' notice count as urgent: subject to availability, with no guarantee and a rush fee. A 96 needs at least 7 days' notice, and shorter isn't offered for a 96. For a client visit or any date that can't move, send the request as soon as the date is set rather than at the deadline.

Cups are made fresh the morning of pickup or delivery, so the date you choose is the day they're made.

Delivery runs on Saturdays to Hamilton, Burlington, Oakville, Mississauga and Toronto, and the fee is part of the total we confirm. Ask for a delivery time in your notes, and make sure someone is on site to receive the cups. See [how Saturday delivery works](/dessert-cups-gta).

Pickup in Hamilton is free, by arrangement. Once your order is confirmed, we share the pickup location with the person who placed it, and a colleague or a courier can collect. For a weekday event, ask about pickup when you send your request. More on [how pickup in Hamilton works](/dessert-cups-hamilton).

Picking up a 24 or a 48 on the 14th? Send your request before 9 AM on the 12th; for a 96, before 9 AM on the 7th. We confirm within the day, and your cups are made fresh that morning. For a Saturday open house with delivery, count back the same way: a 24 or 48 by 9 AM on Thursday, and a 96 by 9 AM the Saturday before.

sections.heading: One contact, one request: what happens next
sections.body:
Office orders go smoothest when one person holds the thread from request to pickup.

1. On [the order page](/order?event=corporate), choose the pack, the size and your flavours, add the date, and pick pickup or delivery. Use the notes for anything we should know, like your event time, a delivery time or any allergies in the room.
2. Send the request. It's a request, not a checkout, so the site takes no payment.
3. We confirm within the day, by email, text or Instagram. A deposit is required to confirm the order, and we explain how to pay it in that reply. For delivery, the fee is included in the total we confirm. For pickup, the location goes to whoever placed the order once it's confirmed.
4. Your cups are made fresh the morning of pickup or delivery. Keep them refrigerated until they go out; they can sit out for about 2 hours.

Put contact details you check during the workday on the request. If your company has its own purchasing process, mention it in your notes.

faqs.q: Can you deliver to our office on a weekday?
faqs.a: Delivery runs on Saturdays, to Hamilton, Burlington, Oakville, Mississauga and Toronto. For a weekday event, ask about pickup in Hamilton when you send your request; a colleague or a courier can collect.

faqs.q: How much notice does a corporate order need?
faqs.a: For a 24 or a 48, at least 48 hours, counted to 9 AM on your pickup or delivery day; under 48 hours is urgent: subject to availability, with no guarantee and a rush fee. A 96 needs at least 7 days' notice, and shorter isn't offered for a 96.

faqs.q: Is there a custom label option for company orders?
faqs.a: The 96 includes a custom label option. Describe what you have in mind in your notes, and we'll confirm what's possible when we reply. A 96 needs at least 7 days' notice.

faqs.q: Can I show the team what the cups look like before we order?
faqs.a: Yes. Each flavour has its own page on [the menu](/menu), and you can follow along on Instagram at @dessertshot.ca.
